issues.description: Template header declares class name 'Image24' but its member declarations use constructors/destructor named 'Bitmap24' (e.g. Bitmap24(), ~Bitmap24()). The implementation file (Bitmap24.cpp) defines methods for class 'Bitmap24' (Bitmap24::Bitmap24, Bitmap24::~Bitmap24). This inner-template inconsistency causes compile/link errors (constructors declared for a different class than implemented) and conflicts with the solution which uses class 'Bitmap24'. Students using the provided template will be blocked from compiling or will be confused about which class to implement/use.
issues.suggested_fix: In the template header (example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) make the class name and its constructor/destructor identifiers consistent with the implementation and the solution. Replace 'class Image24' with 'class Bitmap24' (or rename the constructors/destructor to match Image24 if you intend that name). Prefer matching the solution: declare 'class Bitmap24' and keep the existing Bitmap24()/Bitmap24(int,int)/~Bitmap24() signatures so the header, implementation, and examples compile together.
